thread:
anya-cs: Heads-up — ACME (acct: acme-inc) opened a ticket: embeddings endpoint returning 403 after SSO provisioning of a new service key. They can hit generation endpoints fine but embeddings calls error.
anya-cs: Repro steps from customer:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED' \
  -d '{"model":"embed-large","input":"hello"}'
```
Response:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"missing required scopes","missing_scopes":["embeddings"]}
```
anya-cs: They said the key was provisioned via our SCIM connector (Okta -> SCIM) when they onboarded a new CI service user.

derek-eng: Can you paste the key id or org/key id? I want to check internal audit and the stored scope list.
anya-cs: Key id: key_01F9Z7A2B3C4D5E6
anya-cs: I queried the admin keys API (only metadata redacted):
```
GET /admin/v1/keys/key_01F9Z7A2B3C4D5E6
{
  "id":"key_01F9Z7A2B3C4D5E6",
  "owner":"svc-acme-ci",
  "scopes":["generation,embeddings"],
  "created_by":"okta-scim-provisioner",
  "created_at":"2026-02-14T15:02:31Z"
}
```
eli-se: ahhh — the scope array contains a single string with a comma. Backend expects each scope to be a separate array element. That explains why embeddings check fails (we look for exact string "embeddings").
eli-se: Likely cause: SCIM mapping sent a CSV into the `scopes` attribute instead of an array, or our Terraform/SCIM sync layer serialized incorrectly.
sso-bot: provisioning_event: svc-acme-ci created via SCIM; attributes: {scopes: "generation,embeddings,rerank"}

derek-eng: Quick mitigation options:
 - Patch the key record to split scopes into proper array elements (internal admin API).
 - Or reprovision the service account from Okta with corrected mapping (preferred long-term).
 - If they prefer rotation: create a new key via Console/API with explicit scopes and swap.

derek-eng: Example admin patch we can run (I'll coordinate with infra on audit log):
```
PATCH /admin/v1/keys/key_01F9Z7A2B3C4D5E6
{ "scopes": ["generation","embeddings","rerank"] }
```
anya-cs: Is patching safe w.r.t. audit and existing tokens? Customer asked if rotating is required.
derek-eng: Patching the metadata that controls permission checks is safe — tokens tied to that key id will immediately have the new scope checks. Rotation isn't strictly necessary unless they want a new token string. We should still record an admin action and notify the customer.
eli-se: Also add a guard in the SCIM sync: if scopes is a string containing commas, split on commas and trim whitespace before storing. I'll open a GH issue.
anya-cs: Ok. I told ACME we can do the admin patch if they sign the audit notice, and suggested they update SCIM mapping. They're okay with patch — want minimal downtime.
derek-eng: I'll run the patch now and log it.
derek-eng: PATCH done. Audit id: audit_20260214_3347

derek-eng: Post-patch admin GET shows:
```
"scopes": ["generation","embeddings","rerank"]
```
anya-cs: Customer retried embeddings call and reports success:
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{"data": [ ... embedding vectors ... ]}
```
anya-cs: ACME confirmed no further impact. They will update Okta SCIM mapping and test with a staging sync.
eli-se: Filed GH issue: redwood/scim-sync#612 — add parsing for comma-separated scopes + unit tests.
anya-cs: Marking ticket resolved. Thanks @derek-eng and @eli-se :thumbsup:
sso-bot: ticket_update: ticket-98234 status -> resolved"
